verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. No declaration was found stating the contraction 𝒯_{0,θ} + t_s 𝒯_{0,z} = F(P_c - v_s) itself. It is one rewriting away from a stated theorem: by `stress_eq`, 𝒯_0 = f • (p₁ - a, p₂ - b) with Lean's shearA = a and shearB = -b_s, so with t_s = b/a one has 𝒯_θ + t_s 𝒯_z = f·[(p₁ + (b/a)p₂) - (a + b·(b/a))] = f·(projection p₁ p₂ a b - shearSize a b), the last step being `field_simp; ring` under a ≠ 0 — the identity written out verbatim at LeadingStressWeights.lean:479. The strict inequality is the cone hypothesis v_s < P_c extracted from `true_cone_iff` at line 477 of the same proof, under `FullTrueCone`. What the Lean checks in place of the display is the conclusion the paper draws from it: `stress_ne_zero` proves 𝒯_0 ≠ 0 at every interior point by contradiction — assuming 𝒯_0 = 0 forces p₁ = a and p₂ = b, so projection = shearSize, contradicting v_s < P_c — rather than by forming the contraction and reading off its positivity. The paper's own hypotheses here are an interval [X_-, Y_1] and the preserved cone; the Lean's are the open interval (activeLeft W, activeRight W), η ∈ [-1,1], and f p ≠ 0.
